pr_body:
Used to obtain pairing flags from peer before pairing.
Returns bt_smp_pairing for a given bt_conn during smp_pairing_req or
smp_pairing_rsp, which contains IO caps, OOB, AuthReq and keys config.

This function is available through a public SMP API.

Fixes: #21036

Signed-off-by: Martin Rieva <mrrv@demant.com>
pr_comments:
**All checks are passing now.**

Btw, I intentionally didn't comment on coding style, as I expect you'll take the warnings from checkpatch into account 😉

@jhedberg I thought a lot about your concern regarding the callbacks and I may have been unclear. This is intended to be called during `bt_auth->pairing_confirm()` in smp.c, which is called directly from `smp_pairing_req` and `smp_pairing_rsp`.
I probably mislead you to believe it was during the PairingConfirm command?

@demantmrrv thanks for clarifying, however currently `pairing_confirm` is only used when we are acceptors and the just-works model is used. Otherwise this callback will not get used. So either we need a new callback, or then a Kconfig which forces this callback to be used in the beginning of every pairing procedure. Please see the doxygen documentation in `include/bluetooth/conn.h` for the full details of how this callback is currently defined.
Closing as it will be replaced by a different solution in a new PR

issue_context.title: Add SMP function similar to bt_conn_get_info
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
It is desirable for the app to dynamically filter pairing requests on the `AuthReq` content, in this case the `Bonding_Flags`, to decide whether to accept or reject an attempt. It can be extended with information on IO Caps, OOB, Max Encryption Key Size and Key Distribution fields.
This feature request is a dynamic solution opposing the static proposal in [PR#21002](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/21002) and with optionally much more information.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add a function to the SMP API such as `bt_smp_get_pairing_info(const struct bt_conn *conn, struct bt_smp_pairing_info *info)` that returns information including, but not limited to, AuthReq parameters for a connection. It can also include the rest of the fields available during pairing.
It will be the callers responsibility to call this function at the right time e.g. during `pairing_confirm`. In case the SMP should not expose a public API it can be called from conn.c instead.
This feature can be implemented as an addition to the current API and is functionally non-intrusive.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Besides the static solution in [PR#21002](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/21002) there is currently no way for the app to detect this parameter.

Alternatively, for this particular case, the `pairing_confirm` callback could be extended with a bond_flag parameter similar to `pairing_complete`. This implies an API change.

Second alternative could be to add `void (*pairing_info)(struct bt_conn *conn, struct bt_conn_pairing_info *info)` to `bt_conn_auth_cb` providing additional information during `pairing_req`, `pairing_rsp` and `security_req`.

review_comments: I'm not sure if it is the best idea to put the packet definition in the header file. Maybe we should have a different structure in the API, instead of using a packet definition.

You should probably add a check for preventing calling this API with `conn == NULL` (i.e. an -EINVAL return to the beginning of it) since without it this for-loop would try to peek into invalid entries.
Thanks, just fixed this along with the formatting!
The more correct way to get the smp context is `smp_chan_get`

This is the pairing response, which is not guaranteed to have been set at the same time as the lifetime of the `SMP_FLAG_SEC_REQ`. This flag is set when having received the Security Request, we need the Pairing Response.
Also security request is optional so this might not be set at all.

The flag `SMP_FLAG_PAIRING` is set by the central when it is sending the pairing_request, so that is not correct either.
I think we either have to do `if(atomic_test_bit(smp->flags, SMP_FLAG_PAIRING) && !atomic_test_bit(&smp->allowed_cmds, BT_SMP_CMD_PAIRING_RSP))`, which seems somewhat convoluted. So maybe the best option is to have a new flag which is set when having received the pairing response in `smp_pairing_rsp`.
